title: One hundred people, ten seats
question: Under a burst of 100 concurrent registrations for 10 seats, how many are confirmed?
setup: Capacity 10, waitlist on, 100 distinct participants sent concurrently. The baseline runs the same load through a check-then-insert implementation with no lock, directly against the same database.

environment.transport: In-process HTTP injection into the real Fastify app (no network hop)

variants.label: Naive baseline
variants.summary: Read the count, then insert: 90 people confirmed for 10 seats.

checks.label: One registration per participant
checks.detail: 0 participants with more than one row

checks.label: No idle seat while someone waits

variants.label: EventCore
variants.summary: 10 confirmed, 90 waitlisted in a gapless order.

checks.label: One registration per participant
checks.detail: 0 participants with more than one row

checks.label: No idle seat while someone waits

limits: The baseline bypasses HTTP, so its timings are not comparable with the locked run — only its outcome is.
Latency is measured by the caller and includes waiting for the pool and for the inventory lock.
One machine, one database, one event. This says nothing about throughput across many events.
